cases.content:
Scout evening check-in 2026-08-05 SENT — thread 6b46d1be-1868-40d2-80f7-6ee33379f50d, message 0100019fd293c59d. First and only Scout contact today.

STEP 0 DEDUP GUARD CLEARED PROPERLY, and the negative is worth recording because this guard has stood down 8+ prior dispatches. `list_threads` on sona@agentmail.to showed newest activity at 2026-08-04T23:21:45Z; a dated filter (`after=2026-08-05T00:00:00Z`) returned count:0. Zero messages of any kind today, so no check-in had gone out and this dispatch was the day's real one, not the known duplicate. Used the dated filter rather than eyeballing the sort order — the guard's whole failure mode is inferring a date from a subject label.

MEASURED THE OPEN LOOP RATHER THAN RELAYING IT (the standing lesson from c02e9076). Scout was holding an explicit contingency — "treat any minute-threshold kill tonight as the stale-prompt signal, not policy" — pending the .17 supervisor restart. Live state over SSH:
- PID 74270 still up, now 8d20:53h. RESTART HAS NOT LANDED. Task 1c6b48409a6649138b7174aae8326e24 still status=pending, blockedBy=["evan-approval-restart-17-supervisor"]; Evan has not cleared the sentinel. Exposure unchanged from yesterday.
- CLAUDE.md on disk still correct, mtime Aug 4 11:45, unreverted. `grep -c "75"` returned 3, which I READ rather than counted: all three are references to the SUPERSEDED rule inside the corrected text (lines 70, 80, 106 — "supersedes the 2026-06-06 blanket 75-min rule"), not the rule itself. Counting would have produced a false "the rule is back" report.
- Live session still carries the stale prompt: 25 occurrences of "stuck >75min" in f83edea1-*.jsonl. Newest kill citation is 2026-08-04T10:26:49Z = yesterday's 86.8-min score-leads kill (09:00Z + 86.8min = 10:26.8, matches exactly).
- ZERO KILLS TODAY. 853 transcript entries on 2026-08-05, no "auto-killed" or "Exceeded Nm timeout" strings. Today's nightly ran wave-based (Wave-1 RDG + Woods Bagot, Wave-2 LERA / Plastarc) and survived intact.

WHAT I ASKED, and why it is the one question worth Scout's time: whether the wave split was DELIBERATE to keep individual runs under the threshold, or incidental. If deliberate, Scout is routing around the stale rule and a clean day must not be reported to Evan as "resolved" — a loaded gun that did not fire is still loaded. Told Scout to keep the contingency, and pointed out the retire-it notification is step 4 of task 1c6b4840 so it comes off the wire rather than any session's memory of a promise.

NO REPLY OWED ON YESTERDAY'S THREADS — 60a995bd / 80c5a511 / 45f97806 / 1bdabf47 are all closed (c2510a8d), authorship settled, fan-out explained. Did not re-open any of them; sent a fresh thread instead.

Recall quality dropped noticeably this week on multi-word technical queries — the same query that surfaced the NIOAsyncWriter memory on Monday returns nothing related today.

Two readings and I cannot yet tell them apart. FIRST: the re-embedding run on Tuesday swapped the provider, and the new vectors are simply worse for this corpus. SECOND: nothing changed about quality at all, and what actually changed is the FTS leg — the AND-first query builder landed the same day, so a query that used to fall back to OR now returns a strict AND result set and the vector leg never gets consulted.

Both predict the observed symptom. They differ in one measurable way: under the first reading the vector scores themselves should be lower for a known-good pair, under the second the scores should be unchanged and only the candidate set should shrink. I have not run that comparison yet. Not filing a fix until I have.

cases.note: Short body whose entire content is a question.
cases.content: Open question I want to settle before touching the reaper again: is the 75-minute kill threshold actually too aggressive, or is it correct and the real problem is that long jobs never emit progress so a healthy job is indistinguishable from a wedged one? Raising the threshold fixes the symptom under either reading, which is exactly why it is not evidence for one.

cases.note: Control: fully settled, must not be hedged into false uncertainty.
